In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of statistical potentials of mean force that can be used in conjunction with experimental NMR data to improve the accuracy of Nucleic acid structures determined by NMR spectroscopy.
the development and implementation of new methodologies to improve the accuracy of structures determined by NMR and X-ray crystallography.

the development of novel statistical potentials for the description of nonbonded interactions that can be incorporated into structure refinement protocols and that can improve the accuracy of Nucleic Acid and protein structure determination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DELPHI base-base positioning potential is a significant advance for the field of structure refinement, and that the methodology is generalizable to other types of biomolecular complexes.

, although the DELPHIC pseudopotential is not the panacea to the problem of structure determination of nucleotides, it does represent a significant advance toward the accurate and reliable determination of the three-dimensional structure of nucleotides by NMR spectroscopy.
the use of the DELPHICS base-base positioning potential in the structure determination of nucleotides and nucleic acids is an essential step in the process of obtaining accurate NMR structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DELPHICS approach is a general and powerful tool for improving the accuracy of biomolecular structures determined by NMR spectroscopy.
the DELPHICS base-base positioning potential provides an effective and simple method for improving the accuracy of the NMR structures of nucleic acid molecules.

the DELPHICS program provides a simple and effective way to incorporate the information contained in the Nuclei Acid Database into NMR structure determination and refinement of DNA, RNA, and protein-nucleic acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a database potential of this kind, derived from a large number of high-quality structures, can provide a useful and significant improvement to the accuracy of the structures generated from NMR and other experimental data, especially for nucleic acids.
